headline: Hike path and NVDA risk lead; Warsh speaks today, retail sales Tuesday

what_happened.summary: The Nasdaq-100 closed Fri 13 Nov at 27943.74 (-1.22%) and the S&P 500 at 7561.67 (-0.40%), so tech again fell more than the broad index. The Treasury curve sold off: the 10-year closed at 5.15% (+5.0 bp) and the 2-year at 4.88% (+2.0 bp). Polymarket (prediction-market prices, not CME FedWatch) puts a 25 bps December hike at 87.5% and a 50+ bps hike at 9.2%. Monday-morning headlines (unverified) describe softer futures ahead of NVIDIA earnings and an Anthropic IPO, and some headlines say yields are easing before Fed Chairman Warsh speaks. There are no live prices in the inputs, so this brief does not say where NQ trades now.
what_happened.market_action: Nasdaq-100 -1.22% vs S&P 500 -0.40% on 13 Nov, a gap of -0.82 pct pts. Over the last 5 sessions the Nasdaq-100 is still ahead by 1.03 pct pts, which includes the rebound after the 5 Nov drop of 6.36%. VIX closed at 19.3 (+3.21%), VXN at 29.38 (+2.91%) and VVIX at 101.53 (+4.98%). SKEW fell to 147.14 (-2.01%). COR1M rose to 11.8 (+18.12%), though it is far below its 20.76 on 6 Nov.
what_happened.macro: Rates are the live variable. The 30-year closed at 5.47% (+4.0 bp), and the 10-year real yield was 2.86% (+8.0 bp) on 12 Nov. Breakeven inflation was 2.24%, so the move in yields is mostly real yields, not inflation compensation (engine read). The latest official prints are October CPI +0.35% m/m (prior +0.65%), core CPI +0.3% m/m, PPI final demand +6.52% y/y, unemployment 4.1% (prior 4.2) and payrolls +165.0k (BLS). September core PCE was 3.12% y/y (FRED). High-yield OAS was 3.2 pct pts (-10.0 bp) on 12 Nov, so credit shows no stress.
what_happened.geopolitics: Not covered by official sources. Brent was 92.14 $/bbl (+2.20%) and WTI 89.62 $/bbl on 11 Nov, so the official oil data is stale. Monday headlines (unverified) say oil is rebounding on Middle East supply risk and on Trump questioning the need for an Iran deal. These do not change anything by themselves.
what_happened.company_news: NVIDIA 8-K (primary source, filed 12 Nov): the Board accepted the resignation of CEO Jen-Hsun Huang effective immediately, and CFO Colette Kress is interim CEO while a search runs. Meta 8-K (primary source, filed 12 Nov): completed a multi-tranche euro senior notes offering, with coupons from 4.300% (2031) to 6.400% (2065). Headlines (unverified) frame this week as a test of the AI trade, with NVIDIA earnings and an Anthropic IPO.

driver_reason: The hike path is nearly fully priced by Polymarket (25 bps at 87.5%, 50+ bps at 9.2%), and the 2-year, 10-year and 30-year yields all rose on 13 Nov. Tech fell harder than the broad index on a day when yields rose, which fits a rate-sensitive move (engine read). NVDA is an overlay, not the main driver.
leader_reason: Nasdaq-100 minus S&P 500 was -0.82 pct pts on 13 Nov, and VXN minus VIX is 10.08 pts, so tech is the higher-beta, higher-vol index. The 5-session gap of +1.03 pct pts and COR1M at 11.8, still low, mean the lead is on the downside and index-level correlation is not clearly high yet (engine read).

overlap_with_previous.echo_check: Narrative echo: the NVDA and 'AI trade test' theme and the hike theme repeat across many headlines with no new primary evidence since the 12 Nov 8-K and the unchanged Polymarket odds. A headline saying there is a '100% chance' of a December hike conflicts with Polymarket's 87.5% and is not used. The Cboe posts supplied are older commentary (March 2024 content under a 15 Nov 2026 date) and add no current evidence.

memory_update.running_thesis: Fed hikes and rising yields are the main backdrop: Polymarket has a 25 bps December hike at 87.5% and 50+ bps at 9.2%, with the 10-year at 5.15% and real yields rising. The Nasdaq-100 is the higher-beta index (VXN minus VIX 10.08) and fell 1.22% on 13 Nov vs 0.40% for the S&P 500. NVDA's CEO resigned (8-K), an overlay before earnings. Credit shows no stress (HY OAS 3.2). Next tests: Warsh speech Mon 18:00 CET, retail sales Tue, FOMC minutes Wed. Cboe posts supplied are old content.
